result.title: Learning What to Degrade: A Recoverability-Aware Curriculum for Reliable Smart-Glasses Super-Resolution
result.summary: Degradations in smart-glasses images obscure small text and fine-grained structures needed by vision-language models (VLMs) for visual assistance. We introduce an high-resolution (HR)-referenced semantic evaluation protocol that compares VLM outputs on restored images with those on corresponding HR references. Our evaluation reveals two failure modes: generative SR can synthesize misleading details, whereas restoration-oriented SR can leave critical evidence blurred or ambiguous. These findings motivate improving faithful detail recovery in restoration-oriented SR, where a key training challenge is to provide sufficiently difficult inputs while retaining recoverable visual information. We propose ReDiC (Recoverability-Difficulty Curriculum), which combines a model-independent recoverability proxy with model-relative restoration difficulty to adapt training degradation severity. ReDiC increases severity when inputs are recoverable and restoration is easy, maintains challenging but recoverable conditions, and reduces severity when estimated recoverability is low. It modifies only training degradation generation, leaving the SR architecture and reconstruction objective unchanged. Across NAFNet, SwinIR, and MambaIR, ReDiC improves average PSNR by approximately 2.5 dB and HR-referenced semantic scores by about 3 points over the corresponding baselines on synthetic benchmarks, with further gains confirmed by LLM-based and human evaluations on 200 real smart-glasses captures.

AI.brief_summary: 针对智能眼镜图像的退化修复，提出以高分辨率参考为基准的 VLM 语义评测协议，揭示生成式 SR 会合成误导细节、修复式 SR 会残留模糊证据两类失败模式，并提出 ReDiC 课程：结合与模型无关的可恢复性代理和模型相关的修复难度，仅在训练时自适应调整退化强度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「误导细节 vs 关键证据模糊」的失败划分与 HR 参照语义评测可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据保真度与幻觉的度量方式，按可恢复性调节训练难度的课程思路也可能迁移到视觉旁路或扰动监督的设计。
